objective: Compare the published approximate GDP filter with a valid adaptive RDP fallback only at matched adjacency and finite-q (epsilon,delta) guarantees.

evidence_tier.label: source-authenticated methodological audit plus local implementation check; no matched privacy comparison executed

sources_and_data.citation: Tran et al., f-Differential Privacy Filters: Validity and Approximate Solutions, arXiv:2602.06756v2
relevant_facts: The mechanism relation is a remove-neighbor pair.
The approximate GDP filter is proved only in asymptotic regimes: error Delta=O(sqrt(q_bar)) near q=0 or Delta=O(log(sigma_bar)/sigma_bar) near q=1.
The paper states that the approximation can underestimate privacy loss at realistic subsampling rates.
The finite-q table and Figure 12 are Monte Carlo validation, not a finite-q exact GDP certificate.
The order-one RDP-to-(epsilon,delta) conversion in Theorem G.1 is a separate algebraic conversion and is not a certified finite-q error bound for the GDP approximation.

sources_and_data.citation: Feldman and Zrnic, Individual Privacy Accounting via a Renyi Filter, NeurIPS 2021
sources_and_data.relevant_fact: The RDP filter theorem supports adaptive pre-release stopping when the pathwise sum of conditionally valid per-step RDP charges stays within a fixed-order budget.

observed: The existing fallback uses a revealed-coin per-step RDP upper bound, deliberately conservative relative to a tighter subsampled-Gaussian bound.
The implementation uses ordinary Python floating point and is explicitly documented as not a certified numerical accountant.

The prior one-dimensional boundary diagnostic reported maximum empirical Gaussian-CDF discrepancies 0.0146299851, 0.0281486450, 0.0481296471, and 0.0921804925 at q=0.1, 0.19, 0.3, and 0.5; these are empirical diagnostics, not privacy certificates.
The prior q=0.1 reproduction used one million trajectories per arm and was close to the paper's reported values, but it was not author code or a matched guarantee.

sources_and_data.scope: formula guardrails and adaptive pre-release stopping only

steps: Read the dependency audit and its declared comparison cautions.
Audited the published filter's adjacency definition, asymptotic theorem, finite-q simulation section, and order-one RDP conversion.
Audited the local adaptive RDP reference and ran its focused tests.
Applied the predeclared gate: do not compare active-step or utility outcomes unless both filters have the same adjacency, finite-(epsilon,delta) guarantee, and certified numerical error accounting.

matched_adjacency.status: conceptually alignable from the paper's definition, but not sufficient to make the finite guarantees comparable

method.certification_standard: A numerical comparison would require interval/validated arithmetic or an otherwise proven error enclosure for every relevant conversion and pairwise privacy quantity; Monte Carlo confidence bounds alone do not certify the GDP approximation error.

observed_result_or_blocker.reason: The published GDP filter has no explicit finite-q worst-case (epsilon,delta) error enclosure at the proposed intermediate q values. Its theorem supplies asymptotic big-O errors with no constants sufficient for certification, while the finite-q evidence is simulation. The fallback is theorem-valid for adaptive RDP but its inspected implementation is the deliberately loose revealed-coin bound in ordinary floating point. No verified author implementation, exact pairwise privacy metric, or validated finite-q GDP conversion was available in the inspected repository/source materials.

requirement_status.tighter_proved_per_step_rdp_bound: not met: no tighter bound was implemented and certified in this task; the available local bound is explicitly conservative
requirement_status.certified_finite_q_conversion: not met: the source gives asymptotic GDP error orders and empirical Monte Carlo discrepancies, not a finite-q certified enclosure
requirement_status.author_code_assumptions_or_exact_pairwis: not met: no author-code artifact or exact pairwise metric sufficient to validate the adaptive filter comparison was identified

observed_result_or_blocker.negative_result: The prior finite-q discrepancies cannot be converted into a matched (epsilon,delta) comparison, and raw active-step counts must not be compared at unequal or uncertified guarantees.

uncertainty: The paper's Appendix G.2 scalar-versus-vector convention and zero-history clipping convention remain unverified against author code.
The Monte Carlo DKW intervals quantify sampling noise only; they do not bound model, theorem-remainder, implementation, or floating-point error.
The local RDP formula is mathematically motivated by the cited theorem, but its floating-point values are not machine-certified outward enclosures.
No claim is made about a production implementation, deployed behavior, or an actual privacy undercount.

next_falsifiable_action.action: Obtain a version-pinned author implementation or fully specified scalar/vector and clipping conventions; then implement a certified interval-arithmetic or validated-quadrature accountant for the exact remove-neighbor subsampled-Gaussian pair, including a tighter proved per-step RDP upper bound and an explicit finite-q GDP-to-(epsilon,delta) error enclosure.
preconditions: freeze q, adaptive schedule, budget, target epsilon and delta
use the same remove-neighbor pair and output convention in both filters
record all interval tolerances and rejection/halting rules
next_falsifiable_action.falsification_gate: If the certified finite-q enclosure overlaps or exceeds the valid RDP fallback at the target guarantee, the claim that the approximate GDP filter safely permits more releases is falsified for that regime; if no enclosure can be obtained, retain this infeasibility result.

decision: Publish explicit infeasibility; do not claim comparable guarantees, undercounting, or production impact.
